paper.title: Description of a New Variable-Length Key, 64-Bit Block Cipher (Blowfish)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Blowfish with 16 rounds, with the initial P-array and S-boxes computed as the hex digits of pi (Machin's formula in big-integer fixed point inside the program), reproduces the 34 published ECB known-answer vectors (Eric Young's set)
The 24 published variable-key-length ciphertexts (keys of 1 to 24 bytes, prefixes of F0E1D2C3B4A5968778695A4B3C2D1E0F0011223344556677)
The published 32-byte CBC, 29-byte CFB64 and 29-byte OFB64 ciphertexts

expected_values_source.what: 'Test vectors by Eric Young' for Blowfish, hosted by the cipher's author
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as strings by script from the fetched file; no code was copied

negative_control: built with -DBF_ROUNDS=15 (one Feistel round fewer), 0 of 34 ECB and 0 of 24 variable-key vectors match, CBC/CFB64/OFB64 fail, and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security claims (resistance to cryptanalysis, weak keys, the key-schedule cost argument)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
keys longer than 24 bytes (up to 56 bytes allowed by the paper) and other round counts
each P/S-box word individually against a published table: pi is computed, and only the vectors (which use a large share, not necessarily all, of the 1042 words) check it
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the published Blowfish ciphertexts for 61 single-block cases and 3 chaining-mode cases, with the tables generated from pi. It does not show the security claims hold.
